statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-96232 (GHSA-f8qh-mqg4-9939) is a .NET information disclosure issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF): an out-of-bounds read in XAML and XPS handling can disclose information over a network; the fix blocks unsafe URI fetching and navigation and adds TrueType font protection and XAML nesting-depth limits. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64 as the only affected .NET 10 packages, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f8qh-mqg4-9939, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/480, https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/12024, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, PresentationUI, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder, UIAutomation, wpfgfx, PresentationNative or PenImc assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. What the packages hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material, metadata and documentation: the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade with no WPF code; the PresentationBuildTasks MSBuild task and the other Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop build files (in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in a nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts), which compile XAML at build time and are not the WPF runtime; the WPF and Windows Forms project template packages (Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.ProjectTemplates and Microsoft.Dotnet.WinForms.ProjectTemplates) in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts and in the templates folder of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, which hold only template project, XAML and source files and package metadata; the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Ref and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Internal nupkg files in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which hold only package metadata and no assemblies; the Microsoft.Private.Winforms nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which holds MSBuild props and targets for Windows Forms projects besides its package metadata; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml and System.Xaml.xml) in the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense package in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which hold no code; the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which carries libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.IO.Packaging) and no WPF assembly; and debug symbol files: WindowsBase.pdb beside the facade (in dotnet10-runtime-dbg and in the shared framework and NativeAOT pack held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap), PresentationBuildTasks.pdb beside the build task, and symbols for WindowsBase, PresentationBuildTasks and Microsoft.Private.Winforms in the symbols archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. So the vulnerable WPF code is not in this owner.

CVE-2026-96232 (GHSA-f8qh-mqg4-9939) is a .NET information disclosure issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF): an out-of-bounds read in XAML and XPS handling can disclose information over a network. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64 as the only affected .NET 8 packages, from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31, fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f8qh-mqg4-9939, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/480, https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/12024, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux (linux-musl) from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. We read all 220 packages of the ten builds published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0), every subpackage including the -dbg debug packages, for x86_64 and aarch64, recursing into the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold, and recorded every .NET assembly with its file version and every ELF, PE and Mach-O file. No WPF code is present: no package contains a PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, PresentationUI, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder, UIAutomation, wpfgfx, PresentationNative or PenImc assembly or native library, a PresentationBuildTasks build task, or a Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack, and no package contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file: every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header. The only assemblies with WPF-related names are WindowsBase.dll compatibility facades of 4 KB to 6 KB that ship with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT compiler and reference packs, and in source-build reference packages in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts; they hold no WPF implementation. dotnet8-runtime-artifacts also holds the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg, whose assemblies are libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs, System.Diagnostics.EventLog and System.IO.Packaging) and no WPF assembly, and the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense documentation nupkg, which contains no assembly. WPF is built only for Windows, so this owner does not contain the WPF component.
